full_narration: If nakedness itself causes shame, why did this statue need a removable fig leaf? The body stayed the same; only the rule changed. In 1857, the Victoria and Albert Museum received David's full-size cast. Queen Victoria reportedly objected to the nudity. A proportional plaster fig leaf was made. It covered David during royal visits. His body never changed. We learn modesty rules from our culture. Those rules vary across eras and situations. Same skin, different rule: shame follows learned social boundaries. Follow for more hidden rules shaping us.
